fields.h1: Build an Employee Feedback Form That Routes Every Comment
fields.hero_description: Create an employee feedback form that routes each comment to the person who can act on it and saves it to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Six Parts That Close the Loop on Staff Comments
fields.features_subheading: A template stops at submit. These six pieces carry each comment to an owner and back to the employee who wrote it.
fields.feature_1:
Each topic has a named owner

Equipment notes go to maintenance, pay questions to payroll, and schedule requests to the shift manager. The employee picks a topic and the comment lands with whoever owns it.
fields.feature_2:
A name field people can skip

Ask for a name and leave it optional. Print on the form who reads each note, and an employee deciding whether to sign one knows exactly where it goes before pressing submit.
fields.feature_3:
A status the employee can follow

Each comment moves from Received to Assigned to Done. An employee who leaves an email gets a message at each change and never has to chase HR to find out where it stands.
fields.feature_4:
One question per screen on a phone

Staff who never sit at a desk open the form from a QR code and answer one question at a time. A packer on a 10-minute break can file a note before heading back to the line.
fields.feature_5:
Every comment in a database you own

Responses are saved as rows you can sort by team, topic, and status. A dashboard counts the open comments for each owner, and each owner works from a list of their own.
fields.feature_6:
The full code, in your GitHub

Export the whole codebase to your GitHub repository on paid plans when the form needs to sit inside an internal HR portal. Host it on your own servers and keep building.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Kinds of Comments, Four Owners
fields.tab_content_1:
Every line 3 jam goes to maintenance

Packers at Pellard Foods have no company email, so they scan a QR code by the time clock and choose a topic before they type. One packer wrote that the case sealer on line 3 jams every shift. Equipment notes go to Teodor Vass, the maintenance lead, and this one was marked Assigned before the shift ended.
fields.tab_content_2:
A Stuck blocker returns each week until resolved

Every Wednesday, engineers at Sundell Software answer 3 questions before their Thursday one-on-one: what went well, what is stuck, and what they need. Wren Okafor marked a slow staging server as Stuck. Marisol Teague, her manager, reads it first, and it returns on each week's form until she marks it Resolved.
fields.tab_content_3:
21 of 38 comments named the weekend rotation

Brennor Health drafts policy in the open. Its new on-call policy took comments for 14 days, and each comment named the section it was about. HR sorted the 38 that came in by section and found 21 on section 4, the weekend rotation. That section was rewritten before the policy took effect.
fields.tab_content_4:
After 2 weeks, any score of 2 or lower goes to IT

Kestrow Freight moved its dispatchers to a new routing app. After 2 weeks, each one rated it on a 5-point scale and said what slows them down. A score of 2 or lower sends the comment to Halsey Ruiz, the IT lead. Bo Lindgren gave it a 2 because a reroute takes 4 taps.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Employee Feedback Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up an employee feedback form where each comment reaches its owner and the employee learns what happened.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down who acts on what
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Keep it short enough for a break
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Paste in the questions you use now
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the topics employees raise, such as equipment or pay, and name one person who owns each. Settle that before you write a single question, because a comment on a topic nobody owns sits unread.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for the topic, the comment, and an optional name. Add a rating only where you plan to compare scores, as with a new tool. Someone filling it in on a phone should be done in under 2 minutes.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Describe the form to Emergent in plain English, or paste the questions from the template or paper form you use today. Emergent builds the fields, the topic routing, and the database, and you change any of it by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Post a QR code where staff clock in for anyone without a desk, and send a link by email or Slack to office teams. Show one question per screen for phone users, and a single page for people on laptops.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the statuses a comment moves through and decide who can read each topic. Keep each list of readers short. Pay questions might go to payroll alone, and equipment notes to maintenance and the shift manager.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Ask 5 employees from different teams to file a real comment. Check that each one reached the right owner, that a skipped name field stayed blank, and that every status email arrived before you post the QR code.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Post a short note each month on what came in and what changed, grouped by topic. Name the fixes, like a repaired case sealer or a rewritten policy section, and pull the counts from the dashboard.

faq_plan.q: What is an employee feedback form?
faq_plan.a: An employee feedback form is a form employees use to tell their employer what is working and what is not, whether that is a jammed machine or a draft policy. It stays open year-round instead of running once a year, and each comment lands with someone who can fix the problem.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an employee feedback form?
faq_plan.a: Decide which topics employees will raise and who owns each one. Then describe the form in plain English to Emergent's AI form builder, which builds the fields, the routing by topic, and a database for every response. File a few real comments yourself before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a staff feedback form ask?
faq_plan.a: Start with three questions: what the note is about, what happened or what you suggest, and whether the person wants a reply. Add a name field and make it optional. Ask for a 1-to-5 rating only when you plan to compare scores later, such as a new tool's score after its first month.

faq_plan.q: How is an employee feedback form different from a customer feedback form?
faq_plan.a: They differ in who answers and who follows up. A general feedback form asks customers or visitors about a product or a visit, and replies come from support. An employee feedback form asks staff about their own work. Every topic needs an internal owner, and the form should say who reads it.

faq_plan.q: Who should see the answers on an employee feedback form?
faq_plan.a: Only the people who own a topic, plus whoever runs the form. Send pay questions to payroll alone, and keep a manager out of comments about that manager. With Emergent, every response is saved in a database you own, and you decide who can open each topic.

faq_plan.q: What should happen after someone submits an employee feedback form?
faq_plan.a: The employee should get a confirmation on screen, and the comment should reach its owner the same day. Track each one until it is closed, and email the employee when it changes hands or gets fixed. A weekly list of comments nobody has picked up shows which owners are behind.

faq_plan.q: Is an employee feedback form the same as a performance review?
faq_plan.a: No. A performance review judges one employee's work. Federal rules, for example, define an appraisal as "the process under which performance is reviewed and evaluated." An employee feedback form runs the other way, with staff reporting on the workplace. To score skills against set criteria, use an assessment form.

faq_plan.q: How long should an employee feedback form be?
faq_plan.a: Keep it to 3 to 5 questions with one open text box, which takes about 2 minutes on a phone. Save long question sets for an annual survey. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps, and a short form that people use every day never runs into a limit.

faq_plan.q: Can an employee feedback form work on a phone for staff without a desk?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Post a QR code in the break room or at the loading dock, and the form opens in the phone's browser. Make the topic a tap instead of a typed answer to keep typing short. Emergent can build it as a one-question-per-screen flow, which suits a small screen.

faq_plan.q: Should an employee feedback form also ask about staff preferences?
faq_plan.a: Keep preferences on a separate form. Feedback needs an owner and a status, while preferences such as favorite snacks or how someone likes to be thanked are reference notes for a manager. A favorite things questionnaire collects those, and the two stay easier to read apart.

plan.angle: The top 10 for employee feedback form is a stack of templates (Jotform, SmartSurvey, LimeSurvey, Lattice), two PDFs (Smartsheet, K-State) and question lists (AIHR, involve.me, SurveyMonkey). Each one is a page of rating questions that ends at submit: nobody owns an answer and the employee never hears back. This page treats the form as a standing channel where every comment lands with the person who can act on it and carries a status the employee can follow. It stays clear of periodic engagement and satisfaction scoring, manager ratings and performance reviews, which have their own pages, and shows four everyday uses: floor staff flagging equipment, prep before a one-on-one, comments on a draft policy and feedback two weeks into a new tool.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build an Employee Feedback Form That Routes Every Comment'; hero 'Create an employee feedback form that routes each comment to the person who can act on it and saves it to a database you own.' covers the whole job; howto description is one sentence with the primary.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is templates and question lists; page gives a question set (FAQ 3 'what the note is about, what happened or what you suggest, and whether the person wants a reply'), length guidance (FAQ 8), a 7-step how-to, four worked examples and the performance-review distinction (FAQ 7).

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: 'case sealer on line 3 jams every shift', 'Thursday one-on-one', 'on-call policy took comments for 14 days', 'a reroute takes 4 taps'.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'Packers at Pellard Foods have no company email', 'Brennor Health drafts policy in the open.', 'Equipment notes go to maintenance'.

craft.evidence: One ', so' ending (tab 1) under the cap; sentences short and varied; no blocking craft defects.

voice.evidence: Plain verbs and concrete detail ('A packer on a 10-minute break can file a note before heading back to the line'); no AI tells. Word repetition of 'comment'/'topic' noted.

truth.evidence: Emergent claims map to prompt-build, alerts, conversational, database-owned, code-export, no-caps, free-start. FAQ 7 quote 'the process under which performance is reviewed and evaluated' matches the 5 CFR 430.203 span in domain_sources; not presented as binding on private employers. Bars 4+6+7+21=38 match tab 3.

distinct.evidence: Standing employee-to-employer channel with owners and statuses; no survey/engagement/evaluation/manager-feedback framing in headings; FAQ 7 sends performance scoring elsewhere. Tabs (equipment, 1:1 prep, draft policy, tool rollout) differ from suggestion-form, engagement, pulse and manager-feedback tabs.

findings.quote: Federal rules, for example, define an appraisal as "the process under which performance is reviewed and evaluated."
findings.issue: 5 CFR 430.203 governs federal agency performance management; 'Federal rules' without that scope could be read as a definition binding all employers (rework-checklist #2, source scope). The definition itself is accurate and imposes nothing, so this is a note.
